PUT /api/articles/:slug/comments/:id with body {"comment":{"body":"..."}}. Returns the updated comment in the same wrapper as the other comment routes.

## Rules (values are read from each source, not copied here)
- R1 Author-only edit. Source: deleteComment and updateArticle in app/src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts. No written rule exists.
- R2 Edit time limit. Source: none in the repo. Assumed: no limit.
- R3 Edited mark. Source: Comment.updatedAt in app/src/prisma/schema.prisma. updateArticle sets it explicitly.
- R4 Error shape and status codes. Source: app/src/app/models/http-exception.model.ts and its handler in app/src/main.ts.
- R5 Auth required on writes. Source: app/src/app/routes/article/article.controller.ts.
- R6 Blank body rejected. Source: addComment in article.service.ts.
- R7 Migrations. Source: app/README.md and app/src/prisma/migrations/. None needed.
- R8 Unit tests. Source: app/jest.config.ts, app/project.json, app/src/tests/services/.

## Decisions
- Non-author: deleteComment answers not found, updateArticle answers forbidden. Follow deleteComment: same resource, same route shape.
- The comment must belong to the article in :slug, else not found. Assumed; not in the repo.

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

generator client {
  provider        = "prisma-client-js"
  previewFeatures = []
}

model Article {
  id          Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  slug        String    @unique
  title       String
  description String
  body        String
  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  tagList     Tag[]
  author      User      @relation("UserArticles", fields: [authorId], onDelete: Cascade, references: [id])
  authorId    Int
  favoritedBy User[]    @relation("UserFavorites")
  comments    Comment[]
}

model Comment {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @default(now())
  body      String
  article   Article  @relation(fields: [articleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  articleId Int
  author    User     @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  authorId  Int
}

model Tag {
  id       Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  name     String    @unique
  articles Article[]
}

model User {
  id         Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  email      String    @unique
  username   String    @unique
  password   String
  image      String?   @default("https://api.realworld.io/images/smiley-cyrus.jpeg")
  bio        String?
  articles   Article[] @relation("UserArticles")
  favorites  Article[] @relation("UserFavorites")
  followedBy User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  following  User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  comments   Comment[]
  demo       Boolean   @default(false)
}

The column is not `@updatedAt`, so the service sets it explicitly with `new Date()`, as `updateArticle` does. No migration is needed, because the column already exists. A new column would duplicate the marker. If you want a separate `edited` flag, I can add that as a migration folder.
3. **Error shape:** `main.ts` line 42 sends `err.message` as the JSON body with the status from `errorCode`. The shapes are not uniform. Blank body uses 422 with `{ errors: { body: ["can't be blank"] } }`. Not found uses 404 with `{}`, as `deleteComment` does. Other routes use 403 with `{ message }` and 401 with `{ status, message }`.
4. **Migrations:** Each is a folder `app/src/prisma/migrations/<timestamp>_<name>/migration.sql`. The README applies them with `npx prisma migrate deploy` and generates the client with `npx prisma generate`. This change adds no migration folder.

- **R5 Auth on writes:** `auth.required` on the new route (`article.controller.ts`).
- **R6 Blank body:** rejected with 422 before any database call, as in `addComment`.
- **R7 Migrations:** none needed, since `updatedAt` already exists.
- **R8 Tests:** `app/src/tests/services/`, run with `nx test`.

**Assumption I made:** the comment must belong to the article in `:slug`, or the request gets 404. The spec says this and the repo does not, so it is an assumption.
